correctness.rationale: Choose alpha=7/20. Zero-rich ternary strings are exponentially sparse because alpha exceeds the binomial zero frequency 1/3. For the rest, the inspected recurrence lemmas yield 2^(m-n)n asymptotic to 3^n, so only O(1) recurrence indices occur for each digit length. After fixing the index and the first (1-alpha)n digits, comparable suffixes would give a positive difference M<3^(alpha n+O(1)) but also M bounded below by a constant times (3/2)^n. The exact inequality 3^alpha<3/2 gives a contradiction. The published antichain bound then yields O(3^n/sqrt(n)) per digit length and O(x/sqrt(log x)) globally.

evidence: Klazar--Luca prove the x/sqrt(log x) bound in base 10 and state that small modifications cover every base b>=4.
Their closing remark says the two parameter conditions cannot be simultaneously satisfied for b=3 and that this case seems to require more substantial changes.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader published theorem stops exactly one base short of the present claim, so it does not imply the ternary case. The present large-deviation repair supplies the missing implication.
